reasons: Hiding a link does not protect the page; the protection of the crews page is not visible here.
Language sync errors are silently ignored.

terms.meaning: the stored record of who is currently signed in
a small store in the browser that keeps values between visits
the remembered fact of whether the small-screen menu is open

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in link and route tools, session tools, the sign-out action, state and effect tools, the text lookup, and the language button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the navigation bar needs these to work.
sections.watch_out: The bar depends on LangToggle, so changes there also change the menu.

sections.name: LINKS, Theme
sections.title: Link list and theme type
sections.what: Lists the menu links with their labels, and marks only the crews link as sign-in only. Defines the three theme choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: one list keeps the menu and its filter in one place.
sections.watch_out: Each link path is written here, so renaming a page means editing this list.

sections.name: ThemeToggle
sections.title: Theme toggle
sections.what: A button that cycles through automatic, light and dark. It applies the choice to the page and saves it in the browser's local storage.
sections.why: The comment says the layout script applies any saved theme on first load, so this only updates it afterwards.
sections.watch_out: If storage is blocked, the choice quietly lasts only for the current visit.

sections.name: Navbar
sections.title: Navigation bar
sections.what: Draws the bar: a skip link, the brand, the menu button, the links with the current page marked, the language and theme controls, and the account area. For a signed-in visitor on a new device, it also loads the account language.
sections.why: Likely reason: one navigation for all pages, with labels for screen readers.
sections.watch_out: A failed language load is ignored, so a broken preferences endpoint goes unnoticed.

summary: The top navigation bar on every page, with links, a small-screen menu, language and theme controls, and sign-in or account controls.
purpose: Lets visitors reach the main sections, switch language and theme, and sign in or out.
why: Likely reason: all pages share one navigation.
how: 1. Reads the signed-in session and the current path. 2. Shows the links, filtering out the crews link unless signed in. 3. Tracks whether the small-screen menu is open, and closes it when the page changes. 4. For a signed-in visitor on a new device with no language cookie, loads the account language and sets the cookie if it is Hindi. 5. Shows the language toggle, the theme toggle, and either the account name with sign-out, or sign-in and join buttons.
inputs: The session, the current path, the language, and account preferences from /api/me/preferences.
outputs: The header bar, a sign-out action, and cookie updates.
risks: Hiding the crews link is not access control. The page itself must check sign-in, which is not in this file. Errors from the language sync are hidden.
debug: If a link is missing, check the sign-in state and the filter. If the menu stays open after moving pages, check the path comparison. If the language on a new device is wrong, check the /api/me/preferences reply.
